items.followUp: How does gathering background knowledge help identify the requirements of a problem?

rubric.why: Shows that relevant prior knowledge or information is gathered.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that we collect or use information/knowledge related to the problem.

rubric.why: Explains how that knowledge helps define the problem.
rubric.description: Explain its help in defining the problem
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the information to understanding or clearly defining the problem or its requirements.

modelAnswer: Gain Background Knowledge means collecting relevant information about the problem.
It helps us understand the problem and define its requirements clearly.

items.followUp: What do the Input and Output sections specify in an algorithm for calculating the area of a rectangle?

rubric.why: Identifies what the input notation represents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying it specifies the data or values supplied to the algorithm.

rubric.why: Identifies what the output notation represents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying it specifies the result produced by the algorithm.

modelAnswer: Input notation specifies the data or values supplied to an algorithm.
Output notation specifies the result produced by the algorithm.

items.followUp: What is one example of non-volatile memory?

rubric.why: States what happens to volatile memory when power is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that volatile memory loses its data when the power is switched off.

rubric.why: Contrasts the data retention of non-volatile memory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that non-volatile memory retains its data when power is switched off.

modelAnswer: Volatile memory loses its stored data when the power is switched off.
Non-volatile memory retains its data even when the power is switched off.
